scenes.heading: Protein structure and the proteome
scenes.sub: Shape is everything for a protein
scenes.say: Proteins speed up reactions, carry oxygen, fight infection and hold tissues together. What a protein can do depends on its 3D shape, and that shape comes from the order of its amino acids.
scenes.caption: Proteins speed up reactions, carry oxygen, fight infection and hold tissues together. What a protein can do depends on its 3D shape, and that shape comes from the order of its amino acids.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A necklace of magnetic beads that twists and pulls into a lump
scenes.science: An amino acid chain folds into a 3D shape
scenes.breaks: a necklace sits still, but proteins flex, and secondary structure comes from backbone hydrogen bonds, not the beads.
scenes.say: Picture a necklace of twenty kinds of beads in a set order. Some are magnetic, some hate water, some are charged. Stretches of string twist into spirals and zig-zags. Then beads far apart attract each other and pull the whole necklace into a 3D lump. That's how a protein folds.

scenes.heading: Four levels of structure
scenes.say: Primary structure is the amino acid sequence, held by peptide bonds. Secondary structure is alpha helices and beta pleated sheets. Tertiary is the 3D shape of one chain. Quaternary needs a team: several polypeptides, like haemoglobin's four subunits.

scenes.heading: What holds each level?
scenes.say: Backbone for secondary, R groups for tertiary. Secondary structure is held by hydrogen bonds between backbone atoms. Tertiary comes from R groups: hydrophobic interactions, hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds and disulfide bridges.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A stomach enzyme works well at pH 2 but stops working at pH 8. Explain why.
lines: pH changes the charges on R groups
Ionic and hydrogen bonds are disrupted
Tertiary shape and active site change
scenes.say: Why does a stomach enzyme stop working at pH eight? The pH changes the charges on R groups, disrupting ionic and hydrogen bonds. The tertiary shape changes, so the active site changes. The substrate no longer fits. The enzyme is denatured, but its primary structure is unchanged.

scenes.heading: The proteome
points: All proteins expressed at a given time
Different proteome in each cell type
Changes with age, diet, disease, stress
scenes.say: The proteome is all the proteins a cell, tissue or organism expresses at a given time. Every cell has the same genome, like the same library. But a liver cell and a muscle cell borrow different books, so they have different proteomes.

scenes.heading: The secretory pathway
steps: Rough ER: ribosomes make the protein
scenes.say: Proteins like insulin leave the cell through the secretory pathway. Really Very Good Very Exciting: rough E R, transport vesicle, Golgi, secretory vesicle, exocytosis.
scenes.caption: Proteins like insulin leave the cell through the secretory pathway. Really Very Good Very Exciting: rough ER, transport vesicle, Golgi, secretory vesicle, exocytosis.

points: Sequence decides shape; shape decides function
Rough ER → vesicle → Golgi → vesicle → out
scenes.say: Quick recap. Sequence decides shape, and shape decides function. Know the four levels and their bonds. Denaturing unfolds a protein without breaking peptide bonds. And secreted proteins go from rough E R to Golgi to exocytosis. Now try the practice questions!
